question: Can a contact persist without a flip? LOOP-NET-20261108-001A, Theorem 3, shows a flip suffices; on all 22 Archimedean and Laves tilings a contact persists exactly when it has one (PLANE-PLAIN-20261109-001A, FLIP-RULE-20261109-001A). Is a flip necessary on small maps of any surface?

public_inputs.library: none beyond run.py in this folder.
public_inputs.family: Every rotation system on E = 1 to 5 contacts (every permutation of the 2E darts), connected, with no contact joining a ring to itself; and 400,000 random permutations each at E = 6 and 7 (seed 20261109). Equally spaced rings.
public_inputs.reading: Persistence by the parity of closed walks of length 1 to E + 1; flips and reflections by building the (anti-)automorphism from one dart.

forbidden_inputs: Changing the roster or the hypotheses after seeing results
primary_observable: For each E: maps, contacts, persistent contacts, contacts with a flip, persistent contacts without a flip (and of those, with a reflection), flipped contacts that do not persist.
cheapest_meaningful_control: Every contact with a flip persists (LOOP-NET-20261108-001A, Theorem 3): the count of flipped contacts that do not persist must be 0.
decision_or_followup_rule: Frozen hypothesis H1: on every map with at most five contacts, every persistent contact has a flip. If H1 holds and the samples at 6 and 7 find no exception either, persistence needs a flip on small maps, and a proof for some class is the next step; if a contact persists without a flip, the smallest such map is the first example of persistence by another mechanism, and whether a reflection explains it is read.
stop_rule: Stop when every map of the roster has its readings.
nonclaims: Exploratory and finite: maps to five contacts, and samples at six and seven.
Equally spaced rings only; two-time knots only (A30).
feasibility_disclosure: Nothing of this search was run before freezing; its cost was estimated, not timed.
